label: Personal learning simulation; AI agent executed; prescribed equivalent plasma load, not observed plasma or equipment data
question: With a fixed matching network, how does a prescribed density change affect load impedance, reflected power, bulk absorption and component losses?
hypothesis: Density times 1.5 reduces both bulk R and L to two thirds at fixed geometry and collision frequency. Reflection and absorbed power need not improve; no automatic matching or recipe search.

numerics.time_basis: Independent steady-state phasor solutions; frequency is not transient time
numerics.convention: exp(+j omega t); RMS voltages/currents; SI internal units
numerics.reference: 50 ohm generator reference plane; lossless 50 ohm feed
numerics.boundary: Uniform prescribed bulk R-L and fixed linear two-sheath equivalent C

metric_definition: Primary comparison at exactly 13.56 MHz. Sampled frequency minimum is a diagnostic, not a continuous optimum or chosen recipe.
previous_review: Published RF varied Cp on Nov 16. Nov 25 local-only L comparison is not published. Today uses a different variable and fresh calculations; identical baseline is recomputed, not reused.
source_authority: Included exact source_snapshot; remote Git SHA alone does not represent the dirty local source tree
